name: Tuck hang

technique.setup: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip at shoulder width and straight arms. Pull the shoulders down into an active hang, then bring the knees up to the chest and hold.
cues: Pull the shoulders down away from the ears
Keep the arms locked straight
Knees to chest, tailbone tucked under
Breathe slowly through the hold
mistakes: Bending the elbows to make it feel easier
Shrugging into a passive hang
Swinging the legs up with momentum
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the elbow or shoulder
Pinching at the front of the shoulder
Grip slipping or the hands going numb

media.searchHint: FitnessFAQs front lever progression tuck hang active hang beginner

notes: First step of the front lever tree, a Q2+ skill. Straight-arm work: move at most one step per block.

name: Tuck front lever

technique.setup: Only start once the front lever gate is met (8 pull-ups, 30 s hollow hold). From an active hang with knees tucked, press the bar down with straight arms until the hips rise to bar height and the back is level with the floor.
cues: Press the bar down towards the hips
Lock the elbows straight
Round the upper back slightly, knees to chest
Keep the back level with the floor
mistakes: Bending the arms into a row position
Hips sagging below the shoulders
Holding the breath and grinding to failure
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the elbow or biceps
Pinching at the front of the shoulder
Lower back pain

notes: A 20 s tuck front lever is part of the front lever gate. Straight-arm work: move at most one step per block.

name: Advanced tuck front lever

technique.setup: Start only after a solid 3x30 s tuck front lever. Get into a tuck front lever, then open the hips until the back is flat and the thighs sit at about 90 degrees to the body.
cues: Flatten the back, no rounding
Press the bar down with straight arms
Keep the knees tucked at 90 degrees
Squeeze the glutes to hold the hips up
mistakes: Letting the hips drop as the back flattens
Bending the elbows
Moving up from the tuck too early
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the elbow or biceps
Pinching at the front of the shoulder
Lower back pain

media.searchHint: FitnessFAQs advanced tuck front lever flat back tutorial

notes: Straight-arm work: move at most one step per block.

name: One-leg front lever

technique.setup: Start only after a solid advanced tuck front lever. From the advanced tuck, extend one leg straight out in line with the body while the other stays tucked; switch the extended leg each set.
cues: Reach the straight leg long, toes pointed
Keep the hips level with the shoulders
Press the bar down with locked arms
Switch legs every set
mistakes: Hips piking or sagging as the leg extends
Always extending the same leg
Bending the elbows
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the elbow or biceps
Pinching at the front of the shoulder
Lower back pain

media.searchHint: FitnessFAQs one leg front lever progression

notes: Hard hold: target 3x20 s. Straight-arm work: move at most one step per block.

name: Straddle front lever

technique.setup: Start only after 3x20 s one-leg front lever. Press into a front lever with both legs straight and spread wide; the wider the straddle, the easier it is.
cues: Spread the legs wide and keep them straight
Body in one line from shoulders to hips
Press the bar down with locked arms
Squeeze the glutes and point the toes
mistakes: Piking at the hips
Bending the knees or the elbows
Holding past good form
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the elbow or biceps
Pinching at the front of the shoulder
Lower back pain

notes: Hard hold: target 3x20 s. Straight-arm work: move at most one step per block.

name: Front lever

technique.setup: Start only after 3x20 s straddle front lever. Press into a horizontal hold with the legs straight and together, body in one line under the bar.
cues: Legs together, glutes and toes squeezed
Press the bar down with locked arms
Ribs down, body in one straight line
Hold level with the floor
mistakes: Piking or arching instead of a straight line
Bending the elbows
Kicking up into the hold with momentum
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the elbow or biceps
Pinching at the front of the shoulder
Lower back pain

notes: Hardest hold: target 3x20 s, then switch to maintenance.

name: Band-assisted front lever row

technique.setup: Loop a band over the bar and rest the hips or feet in it from a box. Hold a tuck front lever position under the bar, then row the hips up to the bar and lower slowly back to straight arms.
cues: Keep the body level as you pull
Drive the elbows down to the hips
Touch the bar to the lower chest or belly
Lower slowly to straight arms
mistakes: Hips dropping so it turns into a pull-up
Half reps that stop before straight arms
Using a band too light to keep the body level
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the elbow or shoulder
Pinching at the front of the shoulder

media.searchHint: FitnessFAQs band assisted front lever row tutorial

notes: Accessory for the front lever tree; hitting 3x8 moves to the next lighter band, then tuck front lever rows without a band.

name: Skin the cat

technique.setup: Use a bar low enough that your feet can touch the floor or a box. From an active hang, tuck the knees and slowly rotate backwards through the arms, only as far as the shoulders allow, then come back the same way.
cues: Move slowly, no swinging
Keep the shoulder blades pulled down and engaged
Arms straight the whole way
Stop at the first sign of pinching and come back up
mistakes: Dropping into the bottom with momentum
Relaxing the shoulders into a passive stretch
Going deeper than is comfortable
stopIf: Pinching at the front of the shoulder
Sharp or joint pain in the shoulder, elbow or biceps
Numbness or tingling in the hands

media.searchHint: FitnessFAQs skin the cat tutorial shoulder mobility

notes: First step of the back lever tree, a Q2+ skill. Comfortable skin the cat is part of the back lever gate.

name: German hang

technique.setup: Use a low bar with the feet on the floor or a box for support at first. Rotate back slowly as in skin the cat and hold at the bottom with the arms behind you, only as deep as is comfortable.
cues: Lower in slowly, never drop in
Keep the shoulder blades engaged, not hanging loose
Arms straight, hold at a comfortable depth
Back out at the first sign of pinching
mistakes: Sinking passively into the end range
Holding through pain to reach the time
Coming out of the hold fast or jerky
stopIf: Pinching at the front of the shoulder
Sharp or joint pain in the shoulder, elbow or biceps
Numbness or tingling in the hands

notes: A 20 s German hang is part of the back lever gate, so the target is 3x20 s. Build depth gradually with feet supported.

name: Tuck back lever

technique.setup: Only start once the back lever gate is met (comfortable skin the cat, 20 s German hang, 5 pull-ups). From a German hang, tuck tight and lift the hips until the back is level with the floor, face down.
cues: Arms straight, press the bar towards the hips
Knees tucked tight to the chest
Back level with the floor
Come out the way you went in, slowly
mistakes: Bending the elbows
Hips too low so the shoulders carry everything
Dropping out of the hold
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the elbow or biceps
Pinching at the front of the shoulder
Numbness or tingling in the hands

notes: Straight-arm work with high biceps tendon load: move at most one step per block.

name: Advanced tuck back lever

technique.setup: Start only after a solid 3x30 s tuck back lever. From the tuck back lever, open the hips so the back is flat and the thighs sit at about 90 degrees to the body.
cues: Flatten the back, hips in line with the shoulders
Arms locked straight
Knees bent at 90 degrees
Squeeze the glutes
mistakes: Hips sagging as the back flattens
Bending the elbows
Moving up from the tuck too early
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the elbow or biceps
Pinching at the front of the shoulder
Lower back pain

media.searchHint: FitnessFAQs advanced tuck back lever tutorial

notes: Straight-arm work: move at most one step per block.

name: Straddle back lever

technique.setup: Start only after a solid advanced tuck back lever. From the advanced tuck, extend both legs straight and wide into a straddle, body horizontal and face down.
cues: Legs straight and wide, toes pointed
Body in one line, hips level with the shoulders
Arms locked straight
Squeeze the glutes, ribs down
mistakes: Arching the lower back to hold the legs up
Piking at the hips
Bending the elbows
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the elbow or biceps
Pinching at the front of the shoulder
Lower back pain

notes: Hard hold: target 3x20 s. Straight-arm work: move at most one step per block.

name: Back lever

technique.setup: Start only after 3x20 s straddle back lever. From a German hang, lift into a horizontal face-down hold with the legs straight and together.
cues: Legs together, glutes squeezed
Body in one straight line
Arms locked straight
Lower out slowly the way you came in
mistakes: Arching the lower back
Piking at the hips
Bending the elbows
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the elbow or biceps
Pinching at the front of the shoulder
Lower back pain

notes: Hardest hold: target 3x20 s, then switch to maintenance.

name: Band-assisted muscle-up transition

technique.setup: Only start once the muscle-up gate is met (8-10 strict pull-ups, 10 dips, chest-to-bar pull-ups). Loop a band over the bar, step into it from a box, and pull high to the bar, then lean the chest over and press up to straight arms; step back down to the box to finish.
cues: Pull high, bar to the lower chest
Lean the chest over the bar as the elbows come back
Press up to straight arms at the top
Lower with control and step down to the box
mistakes: Pulling too low so the transition stalls
One arm turning over before the other
Dropping from the top instead of lowering
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the elbow, wrist or shoulder
Pinching at the front of the shoulder

media.searchHint: Calisthenicmovement band assisted muscle up transition tutorial

notes: Q2+ skill. Hitting 3x5 moves to the next lighter band; after the lightest band, go to negatives.

name: Muscle-up negative

technique.setup: Place a box under the bar so you can step up into a straight-arm support on top of the bar. Lower slowly over 3-5 s through the transition and down to straight arms, then step down to the box; never drop from the bar.
cues: Start tall in support, arms straight
Lower slowly through the transition, chest over the bar
Keep the elbows close as you pass under
Step down to the box, never drop
mistakes: Falling through the transition in under 2 s
Dropping off the bar at the bottom
Elbows flaring wide
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the elbow, wrist or shoulder
Pinching at the front of the shoulder

notes: Box height logged so the step-down stays safe. A dip station can be used for the support part only if a box is still underfoot.

name: Bar muscle-up

technique.setup: Hang from the bar with a grip just narrower than shoulder width. Pull explosively high, turn the chest over the bar and press to straight arms, then lower with control back to a hang and step down to a box.
cues: Pull explosively towards the hips, not the chin
Lean the chest over the bar fast
Press up to straight arms
Lower with control, no dropping
mistakes: Kipping or chicken-winging one arm over
Pulling too low to clear the bar
Dropping from the top
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the elbow, wrist or shoulder
Pinching at the front of the shoulder

notes: Low reps on purpose: quality over volume. Do it fresh, at the start of the session.
